integration_decision.name: STALE_GENERATION_ROLLBACK_NOT_PREVENTED_BY_PUBLICATION_ONLY_LOCK
integration_decision.finding: Pinned runner calls load_observations, computes snapshot, then independently replaces latest/audit/anata; ArchiveWriterLock covers archive append/load only. A lock added solely around the three output replacements could fix B/A/A and B/B/A interleaving yet still allow an older A snapshot, computed before rowB was appended, to overwrite a fully published newer B snapshot as coherent A/A/A. Three-file coherence alone is therefore insufficient; acceptance must also reject stale generation rollback. No production race reproduced.
integration_decision.no_network_contract: Spawn child A on empty archive at fixed T. Inside A, wrap runner.load_observations in child process, ACK after the real call returned zero rows, then hold before frame/output publication. In independent child P append PIT-visible rowB and ACK actual append completion (not attempted start). If P completes while A held, spawn unpatched B on same directory; require B's real read/return and persisted three outputs contain rowB (B/B/B) before releasing A. Release A and require bounded completion; final persisted generation must still include rowB and not roll back to A/A/A. The pinned unguarded source is expected to produce RED A/A/A after A resumes. A publication-only lock does not change this expected RED because it starts after A's stale read. If a valid read-through-publish lock prevents P append, require positive observed lock/wait evidence (not just timeout), release A, then require P append and B complete, final B/B/B. Keep existing separately frozen first/last publication-boundary mixed-generation tests, bounded recovery C, returned/persisted source_record_id-to-role checks. Use child-local hooks, Events/Queues, explicit ACKs and finally cleanup, no sleeps as causal oracle, no network. Collect-only + targeted deterministic tests + python -m pytest -q part2/capital_flow/tests at exact SHA.
integration_decision.acceptance_design: Serialization must cover read-through-publish or use a generation/version compare-and-swap that prevents an older snapshot from replacing a newer one. This is an integration acceptance requirement, not an instruction to change Specialist code.
